title: Back and chest, with Maddy: two minutes
steps: A thin layer across the back, chest and shoulders, around open spots.

title: Breakfast
steps: Five eggs over easy, two protein toast, sauteed greens, kimchi.

title: Clay mask (Fridays)
steps: Clay mask on the nose and pores, ten to fifteen minutes.

steps.what: Standing hip flexor lunge, 45 seconds a side, 2 rounds.
steps.sub: Anterior tilt - ED support - 45 sec each side
steps.why: Tight hip flexors are the #1 driver of anterior pelvic tilt and compress the pelvic floor. Releasing them daily targets your tilt, SI pressure, and blood flow through the pelvic region.
cues: Step one foot forward into a lunge. Front knee over ankle, back leg straight.
Keep torso upright and hips square to the front.
Shift forward until you feel a stretch deep in the front of the back hip.
Hold 45 sec. Switch sides. 2 rounds each.

steps.what: Standing figure-4, 45 seconds a side.
steps.sub: SI joint - ED support - 45 sec each side
steps.why: The piriformis sits directly next to the pudendal nerve. A tight piriformis = nerve compression. Also relieves SI joint tension.
cues: Stand near a wall or fence. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Slowly sit back and down until you feel a deep stretch in the glute of the crossed leg.
Keep spine long. Breathe into the stretch.
Hold 45 sec. Switch sides.

steps.what: Standing pelvic tilts, 15 to 20 reps.
steps.sub: Anterior tilt - Low back reset - 60 sec
steps.why: Teaches your pelvis what neutral actually feels like. Living in anterior tilt compresses the SI joint and shortens the pelvic floor chronically.
cues: Feet hip-width, soft knees. Hands on hip bones.
Exaggerate your low back arch (your default anterior tilt).
Tuck tailbone under, squeeze glutes gently, flatten low back.
Rock slowly between the two, finding neutral. 15-20 reps.

steps.what: Standing side bend, 30 seconds a side, 2 rounds.
steps.sub: Full spine - SI joint - QL - 30 sec each side
steps.why: Opens the quadratus lumborum - the muscle that frequently pulls the SI joint out of alignment. Also decompresses the thoracic spine and stretches the lateral shoulder capsule.
cues: Stand tall, feet hip-width. Raise one arm straight overhead, palm facing in.
Lean slowly to the opposite side - feel the stretch from hip through shoulder.
Both feet planted, hips square.
Hold 30 sec each side. 2 rounds each.

steps.what: Cross-body shoulder stretch, 30 seconds a side, 3 rounds.
steps.sub: Posterior capsule - Rotator cuff - 30 sec x3 each side
steps.why: The posterior shoulder capsule is one of the most commonly tight structures in lifters. Tightness causes internal rotation, impingement, and compensatory forward head posture.
cues: Bring one arm across your chest at shoulder height.
Use the opposite hand to support the elbow - gentle pressure inward, not downward.
Feel the stretch in the back of the shoulder. Shoulder blade relaxed and down.
Hold 30 sec. Switch sides. 3 rounds each.

steps.what: Diaphragmatic breath with the pelvic floor release, 8 to 10 breaths.
steps.sub: ED support - Pelvic floor - Nervous system - ~2 min
steps.why: Weightlifters almost universally develop a hypertonic pelvic floor. Deliberate release on the inhale improves blood flow and nerve signaling. Most important move on the list. Pair with Pulsetto.
cues: Stand or sit. One hand on belly, one on chest.
Inhale slowly through nose for 4-5 counts. Belly rises, chest stays still.
As you inhale, consciously let go of your pelvic floor - release downward.
Exhale slowly for 5-6 counts. 8-10 breaths total.

steps.what: Doorway chest opener, 30 seconds, 3 rounds.
steps.sub: Pec minor/major - Anterior shoulder - 30 sec x3
steps.why: Heavy pressing and rowing chronically shortens the pec minor, tilting the scapula forward and internally rotating the shoulder. One of the most prescribed interventions in shoulder rehabilitation.
cues: Stand in a doorframe. Both forearms on the frame, elbows at 90 degrees.
Step one foot through and shift forward until you feel the stretch.
Core lightly engaged - avoid arching the low back.
Hold 30 sec. Rest 10 sec. Repeat 3 rounds.

steps.what: Standing thoracic extension, 10 to 12 reps.
steps.sub: Upper back - T-spine mobility - Shoulder overhead path - 60 sec
steps.why: Thoracic kyphosis is the single biggest limiter of overhead pressing range and a major driver of shoulder impingement. Daily T-spine extension is one of the highest-value shoulder investments on this list.
cues: Stand tall. Interlace hands behind head, elbows wide.
Gently draw elbows back and open chest toward ceiling. Mid-back is the hinge point.
Hold 2-3 seconds, breathing into the stretch. Return to neutral. 10-12 reps.
Keep low back relaxed - this is thoracic extension, not lumbar.

steps.what: Phone face down first. No news, no email, no scroll.
steps.why: Cortisol peaks 20 to 30 minutes after waking, and phone contact there derails the whole day.
cues: Set the phone down, screen to the table. No news, no email, no scroll.

steps.what: Shower and teeth. Nothing to decide, the order is already set.
cues: Warm shower, brush teeth. Nothing to decide, the order is already set.

steps.what: The hum: in the shower, 30 seconds, low and steady.
steps.why: Humming vibrates the throat and stimulates the vagus nerve directly.
cues: In the shower, hum for 30 seconds. Low and steady.

steps.what: Face and simple skin: cleanse, moisturise.
cues: Cleanse, moisturise. Quick and kind. Done is clean, not perfect.

steps.what: Supine figure-4 hip release, 60 seconds a side.
steps.sub: SI joint - Pelvic floor - 60 sec each side
steps.why: Same piriformis release as the morning, but lying down - gravity-assisted and deeper. Excellent for resetting SI joint tension from the day and gym.
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Either stay here if you feel stretch, or gently draw both legs toward your chest.
Breathe slowly into the stretch. Let the floor hold you.
Hold 60 sec. Switch sides.

steps.what: Supine spinal twist, 60 seconds a side.
steps.sub: Low back - SI joint - 60 sec each side
steps.why: Decompresses the lumbar spine, releases the SI joint, and gently massages the digestive organs. Completely passive end-of-day reset.
cues: Lie on your back. Draw one knee to your chest.
Gently guide that knee across your body toward the floor on the opposite side.
Extend same-side arm at shoulder height. Look away from the knee.
Hold 60 sec. Switch sides.

steps.what: Child's pose, 90 seconds.
steps.sub: Full spine - Hip flexors - Low back - 90 sec
steps.why: Lengthens the entire posterior chain and activates the parasympathetic nervous system through gentle forward folding.
cues: From kneeling, sink hips back toward heels.
Walk hands forward until you feel a gentle stretch. Arms relaxed.
Rest forehead on floor or pillow. Soften everything.
Hold 90 sec. Breathe deeply into your lower back.

steps.what: Tier 1, the diaphragmatic reset: in 4, pause 1, out 6 to 8.
steps.sub: Tier 1 - Foundation - Daily - 5 minutes, lying on your back, knees bent, feet flat
steps.why: The foundation. The exhale is the master key: it tells the nervous system the day is safe.
cues: Inhale through your nose for 4 counts. Belly rises, chest stays still.
Pause at the top for 1 count.
Exhale through your nose for 6-8 counts. Belly softens.
On the inhale, invite your perineum to drop. On the exhale, let it gently return to neutral. Not a Kegel: you are removing the chronic grip.
Target: 10-15 breath cycles, about 5 minutes.

steps.what: Tier 2, the extended exhale: in 4, out 6 to 8, by the week.
steps.sub: Tier 2 - Vagus nerve - Add after 1-2 weeks
steps.why: Exhaling longer than you inhale is one of the most direct ways to activate the vagus nerve.
cues: Weeks 1-2: inhale 4, exhale 6.
Weeks 3-4: inhale 4, exhale 7.
Week 5 and on: inhale 4, exhale 8.
Do not rush to the 1:2 ratio. The nervous system needs time to trust it.

steps.what: Tier 3, the 0.1 Hz protocol: in 5, out 5, ten minutes.
steps.sub: Tier 3 - Resonance - Add when Tier 2 feels natural
steps.why: About 6 breaths per minute. Amplifies heart rate variability; used in clinical HRV training.
cues: Inhale 5 counts, exhale 5 counts. 6 breaths per minute.
Add pelvic floor coordination: notice on the inhale, consciously release and drop on the exhale.
Duration: 10 minutes.

steps.what: Cetaphil cleanser.
cues: Remove the day: sunscreen, sebum, environmental particulates.

steps.what: CeraVe resurfacing retinol serum, pea sized, on the ramp's nights.
steps.why: The twenty minute wait is not real, and a twenty minute stall is what kills a 10pm routine.
cues: Pea sized, whole face. Apply about sixty seconds after towel drying, to skin that feels dry.

steps.what: Brickell eye cream, ring finger, along the orbital bone.
cues: After the retinol, before the moisturizer. Wash hands first. Ring finger only, tap along the orbital bone from the outer corner inward.

steps.what: Cetaphil lotion.
cues: Lock in moisture after the retinol. Seals the barrier and reduces flaking.
